# Crux

> Crux is an open-source Go CLI that orchestrates multiple AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI) running in parallel tmux sessions. It enforces phase-based execution with a two-document system (spec + prompt doc), three-layer persistent memory (markdown bank, SQLite with FTS5, chromem-go vector index), verification gates (go build/vet/test must pass before advancing), and four-tier security sandboxing. Single binary, no CGO, MIT licensed.

Crux automates the workflow: Plan → Write prompt docs → Execute with agents → Verify → Commit. Instead of a human pasting context and running checks, Crux does this for every agent, every prompt, every session. Agents communicate via tmux send-keys/capture-pane with JSON message envelopes. The orchestrator polls panes every 1-2 seconds, tracks world state, and uses Decision RAG (vector search over past decisions) to make coordination choices.

Key technical constraints: all code compiles with CGO_ENABLED=0, SQLite via ncruces/go-sqlite3 (WASM-based), vector search via chromem-go (embedded, no external services), embeddings via Ollama or cloud providers (OpenAI, Google, Cohere).

## Docs

- [Getting Started](https://runcrux.dev/docs/getting-started/installation): Installation, quick start, first project walkthrough
- [Architecture](https://runcrux.dev/docs/concepts/architecture): Core architecture reference — orchestrator loop, agent plugins, memory system, security model
- [Phase System](https://runcrux.dev/docs/concepts/phase-system): Two-document system (phase spec + prompt doc), phase engine, dependency graph, verification gates
- [Memory System](https://runcrux.dev/docs/concepts/memory): Three-layer memory — markdown bank, SQLite operational store with FTS5, chromem-go vector index
- [Security Model](https://runcrux.dev/docs/concepts/security): Four-tier permissions (readonly/standard/elevated/autonomous), filesystem sandbox, audit logging, rate limiting
- [Configuration](https://runcrux.dev/docs/reference/configuration): YAML config reference, all fields with types and defaults, environment variable overrides
- [CLI Reference](https://runcrux.dev/docs/reference/cli): All commands — init, start, status, phase, decisions, notes, replay, audit, plan, instruct, prefs
- [Writing Phases](https://runcrux.dev/docs/guides/writing-phases): How to write phase specs and prompt docs, decomposition heuristics, exit criteria rules
- [Multi-Agent Workflows](https://runcrux.dev/docs/guides/multi-agent): Running parallel agents, file scope validation, branch management, conflict detection
- [Custom Plugins](https://runcrux.dev/docs/guides/custom-plugins): Building an AgentPlugin implementation — LaunchCmd, DetectReady, DetectBusy, FormatMessage, ParseOutput

## API

- [AgentPlugin Interface](https://runcrux.dev/docs/reference/agent-plugin): Go interface that each CLI tool implements — Name, LaunchCmd, DetectReady, DetectBusy, DetectError, DetectRateLimit, FormatMessage, ParseOutput, Capabilities
- [Phase Spec Format](https://runcrux.dev/docs/reference/phase-spec-format): Status, Depends On, Design Rationale, Tasks (by prompt), Files (New/Modified/Referenced), Exit Criteria
- [Prompt Doc Format](https://runcrux.dev/docs/reference/prompt-doc-format): Required Reading, Interface Contract, Task, Verification, Acceptance Criteria, Stop Rule per prompt
- [Message Protocol](https://runcrux.dev/docs/reference/message-protocol): JSON envelope format for orchestrator-agent communication over tmux

## Optional

- [Telegram Integration](https://runcrux.dev/docs/guides/telegram): Telegram bot for remote monitoring, notifications, and approval workflows
- [MCP Server Registry](https://runcrux.dev/docs/guides/mcp-registry): Parse and register MCP servers from Claude/Codex/Gemini configs for tool-aware task routing
- [Troubleshooting](https://runcrux.dev/docs/troubleshooting): Common issues — agent detection, gate failures, rate limits, tmux sessions, SQLite locking, vector search
- [Contributing](https://runcrux.dev/docs/contributing): Development setup, code conventions, PR process, architecture decisions
